name: Dental work / teeth maxxing

lead: Teeth maxxing means improving how teeth look, mostly by whitening them with strips, pastes, trays or dentist treatments, often alongside orthodontics and other dental work. The payoff is a brighter, tidier smile that is visible after use.

The chain is direct: hydrogen peroxide or carbamide peroxide breaks down pigment molecules in the tooth, lightening its shade, while whitening toothpastes mainly remove surface stains with abrasives. Randomized trials and reviews show peroxide whitening changes tooth colour. Forum users also discuss DIY methods that have not been studied.

paras: Options range from over-the-counter strips and toothpastes to custom trays and in-office dentist treatments. Many people combine whitening with a cleaning, orthodontics or cosmetic dental work. Shade changes appear over days to weeks of use, depending on the product.
Tooth sensitivity is frequently reported, and strong peroxide can irritate or burn gums. Regulators limit peroxide strength in retail products, and over-abrasive products can damage tooth tissue.

angle.text: You whiten teeth with strips, pastes and dentist treatments, often alongside orthodontics, for a brighter and neater smile. Peroxide whitening breaks down tooth pigment, and the shade change is visible after use. Trials and reviews have measured colour change with peroxide products.

lead: Dental work, or teeth maxxing, is the looksmaxxing practice of improving how the teeth and smile look. It spans colour (whitening), position (braces and clear aligners), shape and size (bonding, enamel reshaping, veneers, crowns) and gum line (gum contouring). Teeth are part of the lower face that is visible whenever someone smiles or speaks, so people in appearance communities treat them as an area where relatively accessible changes can alter overall facial impression [1][2][3].

Whitening is the most discussed and most commonly performed cosmetic dental treatment. It uses hydrogen peroxide or carbamide peroxide to break down pigment molecules in and on the tooth [4][3]. Straightening uses fixed braces or removable clear aligners to move teeth over months to a few years [5][6][7]. Veneers and bonding add a thin layer of porcelain or composite resin to change colour, shape and apparent alignment, including in the "Hollywood smile" makeovers that dentists describe [8][9].

Research on the topic includes randomized trials and systematic reviews of peroxide whitening, reviews of clear aligner effectiveness, and long-term follow-up studies of veneers [10][7]. Regulators set limits on peroxide strength in retail products, and professional bodies have raised concerns about untrained whitening providers, mail-order aligners and overseas cosmetic dental packages [4][7][11][12]. In forum discussion, a large share of threads concern whitening strips, staining from coffee, sensitivity, and a widely shared DIY whitening guide [1][1][13][14].

paras: Cosmetic dentistry as Wikipedia describes it covers work meant to improve the look of teeth, gums or bite, often without changing function. Common procedures include whitening, enamel reshaping, bonding, bridges, veneers, implants, gum lifts and straightening [3]. Prosthodontics and orthodontics are the two specialties most focused on aesthetics, while the American Dental Association does not recognise cosmetic dentistry itself as a specialty and many dentists use the label "cosmetic dentist" regardless of training [3].

In looksmaxxing communities, teeth work is usually grouped into three layers: colour (whitening), alignment (braces or aligners, sometimes with jaw work) and shape or coverage (bonding and veneers). Posters often treat whitening as a first, low-cost step and orthodontics or veneers as larger investments [1][2].

Tooth colour depends on enamel thickness and mineral content, the colour of the underlying dentine, and lighting. Teeth darken with age as secondary dentine forms and enamel wears thin [4]. Extrinsic stains sit on the surface and come from tobacco, coffee, tea, red wine, curries and some mouthwashes; intrinsic stains arise within the tooth from ageing, decay, trauma, fluorosis, certain antibiotics such as tetracycline and other causes [4]. Surface stains can be removed by professional cleaning or whitening toothpaste, whereas intrinsic stains generally cannot be removed mechanically and may be covered with bonding or veneers [4].

In-office gels are described as roughly 10-44% carbamide peroxide (about 3-16% hydrogen peroxide), with some light-accelerated systems using 25-38% hydrogen peroxide; sessions can shift shade by 2 to 7 shades [4]. Wikipedia reports that a 2015 study found light activation did not improve bleaching and could raise tissue temperature [4].

At-home options include strips (commonly used twice daily over about two weeks, lightening 1-2 shades), brush-on gels, rinses, custom trays worn with carbamide peroxide gel overnight or for a few hours a day, and whitening toothpastes that rely on abrasives, detergents and sometimes low peroxide levels for 1-2 shades of lightening [4]. Baking soda toothpaste is described as low-abrasive and effective for stain removal, with no adverse effects found in the clinical studies cited [4]. Newer peroxide-free agents such as phthalimidoperoxycaproic acid (PAP) are described as causing little enamel change [4].

Whitening works best on yellow teeth and least on grey ones, and does not change porcelain, ceramics, gold or existing fillings [4]. Wikipedia notes that nearly half the colour change from a one-hour in-office treatment may be lost within a week as dehydration-related whitening reverses, and that stains can return within a couple of months, with retreatment often needed every six months to a year, more often for smokers and heavy coffee drinkers [4]. Dentists commonly suggest drinking staining liquids through a straw, rinsing after meals and avoiding staining foods for 24-48 hours after treatment [4].

Orthodontics is the specialty concerned with misaligned teeth and jaws. Wikipedia traces attempts at tooth straightening to about 1000 BC, and describes modern orthodontics as taking shape in the mid-1800s with Norman Kingsley's Oral Deformities and Edward Angle's malocclusion classification, with Angle called the "father of modern orthodontics" [5]. Pierre Fauchard published on straightening teeth in 1728, nickel-titanium wires entered orthodontic use in 1979, bonded brackets replaced wrapped bands in the mid-1970s, and Lawrence Andrews introduced the straight-wire appliance in 1976 [5][6].

Fixed braces use brackets bonded to the teeth, joined by wires; adjustments are typically every few weeks, and treatment commonly takes from six months to about two and a half years [5][6]. Variants include ceramic or nearly transparent brackets, gold-plated steel for nickel allergy, self-ligating brackets and lingual braces bonded behind the teeth so they are not visible from the front [6]. After treatment, retainers are usually worn long term; Wikipedia states that over half of patients show some reversion within ten years [5]. Adults use braces as well as teenagers; palatal expansion in adults generally needs surgery because the palate bones have fused [6].

Clear aligners are removable transparent plastic trays made from digital models of the teeth, each worn about 22 hours a day for one to two weeks; the average treatment lasts roughly 13.5 months [7]. Align Technology, maker of Invisalign, was founded in 1997 by Zia Chishti, who conceived the design during his own orthodontic treatment, and US sales began in 1999 [7]. Aligners are indicated for mild to moderate crowding and spacing, and are described as less effective than fixed braces for significant rotations and some other movements [7]. Wikipedia cites a 2014 systematic review that found study quality insufficient for firm conclusions on effectiveness [7].

Direct-to-consumer aligner companies expanded the market. SmileDirectClub launched in 2014 with at-home impression kits and remote review by licensed dental professionals, went public in September 2019 and was operating around 300 retail locations in the US, Canada, Australia and the UK before filing for bankruptcy in September 2023 and ceasing operations that December [12]. The American Association of Orthodontists issued a consumer alert on mail-order aligners and filed complaints with 36 state dental boards, while the company disputed those characterisations, and a 2020 CBC investigation reported questionable treatment plans [7][12].

Dental bonding applies tooth-coloured composite resin to the tooth, which is shaped and hardened with blue light. Irwin Smigel is credited as an early adopter of using it to close gaps, lengthen teeth and recontour the smile instead of using crowns [9]. Enamel reshaping removes small amounts of enamel to change length or fix chips, and gum lifts reshape gum tissue so teeth look longer or more symmetrical [3].

A veneer is a layer of composite or porcelain placed over a tooth to change its appearance. Composite can be placed directly or made indirectly, and is described as lasting around four years; porcelain is made indirectly, is more stain-resistant, and typically lasts 10-30 years with modern bonding [8]. Ultra-thin "no-prep" porcelain laminates need little or no tooth reduction, whereas conventional veneers usually require shaving some enamel, with estimates of 3-30% of tooth surface removed [8]. Uses listed include covering teeth that will not whiten, closing gaps, lengthening worn teeth, and evening colour, shape and symmetry for "Hollywood" smile makeovers [8].

Wikipedia reports a cited study in which about half of veneers had been displaced, needed re-treatment or were unsatisfactory after ten years, while other longitudinal studies show high survival with careful case selection and maintenance [8]. Canadian dentist Michael Zuk has criticised overuse of porcelain veneers as "instant orthodontics" on healthy young teeth, and leading dentists caution that minor wear does not justify them [8]. The founder of aesthetic dentistry is often considered to be Newell Sill Jenkins, who developed a porcelain enamel and advanced porcelain inlays, crowns and bridges in the 19th century [3].

Dental tourism is travel abroad for lower-cost dentistry. Wikipedia lists Turkey as a hub for veneers, crowns and implants, Hungary as a dental destination (Mosonmagyaróvár had about 350 clinics in 2015), and Mexico, where Los Algodones near the US border has roughly 600 dentists serving mainly tourists [11]. Veneers are sometimes nicknamed "Turkey teeth" [8]. Risks listed for medical tourism in general include variable aftercare, limited follow-up once home, limited legal recourse and insurance gaps [11].

A 2023 systematic review examined the prognosis of at-home bleaching with low-concentration products, and a controlled trial in adolescents compared hydrogen peroxide products with placebo over a 12-month follow-up, assessing colour change, sensitivity and discomfort. A critical review of modern whitening concepts and a review of natural whitening ingredients are also published [10]. A review cited on Wikipedia found whitening improved oral health-related quality of life in aesthetic areas in young participants, while tooth sensitivity reduced it [4].

For orthodontics, Wikipedia states that patients who completed treatment reported higher quality of life than untreated patients undergoing treatment, and a Cochrane review found no high-quality evidence on managing relapse of lower front teeth [5][7].

Whitening: Wikipedia reports sensitivity in 67-78% of in-office patients lasting 4-39 days, less with home use; peroxide at 10% or above can burn gums, especially with poorly fitting trays; and over-bleaching can give a translucent look [4]. A review of natural whitening states high-concentration peroxide products can demineralise through oxidation, whereas natural ingredients lighten without eroding surfaces. Very abrasive toothpastes can harm dental tissue [4]. Wikipedia also describes "bleachorexia", an obsessive pattern of repeated whitening, and lists contraindications including age under 16, pregnancy or lactation, gum recession, cracks and untreated decay [4]. The IARC found insufficient evidence that hydrogen peroxide is a human carcinogen [4].

Braces and aligners: fixed appliances can increase plaque, gingivitis and gum recession, pain after adjustments is very common, and most treatments cause some root resorption, rarely severe [6]. Poor hygiene during treatment can cause decalcification and decay [5]. Veneers: sensitivity and decay can occur even when done properly, and replacement is a recurring cost [8].

In the EU, retail whitening products are limited to 0.1% hydrogen peroxide, with 0.1-6% allowed only via dental professionals for patients aged 18 and over; the US FDA endorses gels up to 6% hydrogen peroxide or 16% carbamide peroxide [4]. In 2010 the UK General Dental Council raised concerns about whitening by untrained staff, and the Tooth Whitening Information Group was founded to provide information [4]. An editorial in the British Dental Journal addresses illegal teeth whitening. In the US, over 100 million people have whitened their teeth, with about $15 billion spent in 2010 per Wikipedia [4].

On looksmax.org users ask about whitening strips, coffee staining, tooth sensitivity and cheaper alternatives [1][1]. In one thread a user reports strips were too painful to keep on for five minutes, and replies suggest coconut oil or a forum member's DIY whitening guide [1]. Other threads discuss whether that DIY procedure worked [13][14]. Dental authorities and the research cited here address professionally supervised methods; they do not evaluate forum DIY protocols.

Randomized trials and systematic reviews of tooth whitening exist [10], and reviews of aligner and veneer outcomes are summarised above [8][7]. They evaluate commercial and professional products, not forum DIY protocols; no studies were found of the DIY methods discussed on looksmax.org.

lore.intro: Whitening is a recurring looksmax.org topic, with threads comparing strips, toothpaste, dentist treatments and a widely referenced DIY guide; veneers and orthodontics appear as larger-ticket options [1][1][13][14].

claims.claim: Whitening strips and pastes are ineffective compared with a DIY method
Natural remedies such as coconut oil or baking soda whiten teeth
Yellow teeth that do not respond to whitening may be due to thick or thin enamel and need other work
Whitening results are permanent once achieved
Clear aligners work as well as braces for any case
Veneers abroad deliver the same result at lower cost
